subject.title: Expose structured progress metrics in hook events for plugin-based live progress cards

question: Should OpenClaw add structured progress metrics to existing plugin hook events, and which runtime source owns step totals, percentages, ETA, and terminal-state values?
rationale: The change is additive at the type level but creates public Plugin SDK semantics that live progress cards may treat as authoritative, so automation should not choose the metric source or absent-value contract alone.

options.title: Define narrow hook metrics
options.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document absent unknowns, and test each affected hook producer.

options.title: Keep phase-only hooks
options.body: Leave plugins to derive textual or phase progress from current tool and lifecycle hooks until OpenClaw has a stronger progress source of truth.

options.title: Create a progress event
options.body: Design a dedicated progress event or agent-event projection instead of attaching percentages to existing tool and terminal hooks.

recommendation.title: Define narrow hook metrics
recommendation.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document absent unknowns, and test each affected hook producer.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal for the public hook contract shape points to vincentkoc.
